newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ASDA H2 margin "similar" to H1.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ASDA H2 margin "similar" to H1.

text.p: British supermarket group ASDA Group Plc expects second half margins to be at similar levels to the first half of the year, chief executive Allan Leighton told Reuters in an interview.
"They should be running at about the same levels in the second half...down...a smidgeon," he said.
ASDA said in a statement that there had been "a modest investment" in gross margin in the first half in order to keep it as one of the lowest price suppliers.
Leighton said much of the impact had come from petrol, where a price war has been waged between supermarkets and oil firms.
But he said operating profits for the first half had shown "even higher growth" than sales, which was encouraging.

ASDA said sales from existing stores rose 10.2 percent in the first half, with total turnover of 3,452 million stg compared with 3,044 million stg, while operating profit was 167.3 million stg, up from 140.5 million stg.
"Being focused on the basics has turned in a good set of results," Leighton said.
He said the company aimed to open around seven stores a year for the next two to three years, as it aims to open seven in the second half of this year.
These would all be large, "market-hall" type supermarkets, he said, because of the need for a "critical mass" of space to drive growth markets of fresh food, entertainment, clothing and healthcare.

ASDA remained "under no pressure to launch" a loyalty card throughout the country, Leighton said, even though the other three major supermarkets -- J. Sainsbury, Tesco and Safeway -- have all started schemes nationwide.
ASDA is testing a card in several stores but Leighton said ASDA customers tended to focus on price, quality and service.
He said ASDA was watching "with interest" moves by its competitors into financial services but felt the focus should be on core values.
"We are shopkeepers, not surfers...waiting for the next big wave," he said.
